claim: Wiz was identified in a mouse screen for epigenetic modifiers.
source: We previously identified Wiz in a mouse screen for epigenetic modifiers.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is a direct assertion about the discovery of Wiz.

claim: Wiz is generally considered a transcriptional repressor due to its association with G9a/GLP.
source: Due to its known association with G9a/GLP, Wiz is generally considered a transcriptional repressor.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about Wiz function based on its protein interactions.

claim: Wiz may also function as a transcriptional activator.
source: Here, we provide evidence that it may also function as a transcriptional activator.
evidence: This is a primary claim of the manuscript supported by multiple lines of evidence presented in the results.

claim: Wiz levels are high in the brain.
source: Wiz levels are high in the brain, but its function and direct targets are unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citation to previous work (Matsumoto et al., 1998) in the introduction.

claim: Wiz peaks were found at promoters in adult cerebellum.
source: ChIP-seq was performed in adult cerebellum and Wiz peaks were found at promoters and transcription factor CTCF binding sites.
evidence: This is directly supported by ChIP-seq experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Wiz peaks were found at CTCF binding sites in adult cerebellum.
source: ChIP-seq was performed in adult cerebellum and Wiz peaks were found at promoters and transcription factor CTCF binding sites.
evidence: This is directly supported by ChIP-seq experimental data and comparison with ENCODE CTCF data.

claim: Genes were differentially regulated in adult cerebellum of Wiz mutant mice.
source: RNA-seq in Wiz mutant mice identified genes differentially regulated in adult cerebellum and embryonic brain.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data presented in the results section.

claim: Genes were differentially regulated in embryonic brain of Wiz mutant mice.
source: RNA-seq in Wiz mutant mice identified genes differentially regulated in adult cerebellum and embryonic brain.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data presented in the results section.

claim: Most genes differentially expressed in embryonic brain decreased in expression in Wiz mutants.
source: In embryonic brain most decreased in expression and included clustered protocadherin genes.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing 31/36 genes decreased in males and 43/44 decreased in females.

claim: Clustered protocadherin genes decreased in expression in embryonic brain of Wiz mutants.
source: In embryonic brain most decreased in expression and included clustered protocadherin genes.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data identifying multiple protocadherin β genes as differentially expressed.

claim: Clustered protocadherin genes decreased in expression in adult cerebellum of Wiz mutants.
source: These also decreased in adult cerebellum and showed strong Wiz ChIP-seq enrichment.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data in adult cerebellum showing decreased expression of protocadherin genes.

claim: Protocadherin genes showed strong Wiz ChIP-seq enrichment.
source: These also decreased in adult cerebellum and showed strong Wiz ChIP-seq enrichment.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing Wiz binding at protocadherin promoters and enhancers.

claim: A precise pattern of protocadherin gene expression is required for neuronal development.
source: Because a precise pattern of protocadherin gene expression is required for neuronal development, behavioural tests were carried out on mutant mice, revealing an anxiety-like phenotype.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge that motivated the behavioral experiments.

claim: Wiz mutant mice display an anxiety-like phenotype.
source: Because a precise pattern of protocadherin gene expression is required for neuronal development, behavioural tests were carried out on mutant mice, revealing an anxiety-like phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data from elevated plus maze and light-dark box tests.

claim: This is the first evidence of a role for Wiz in neural function.
source: This is the first evidence of a role for Wiz in neural function.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings, based on the absence of prior reports.

claim: The MommeD30 mutation in Wiz is a single base pair deletion of an adenine.
source: The mutation underlying the MommeD30 strain was found to be a single base pair deletion in the gene Widely interspaced zinc finger motifs, Wiz. The deletion, of an adenine, causes a frame-shift that introduces a premature stop codon.
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data from the original identification of the mutation.

claim: The MommeD30 mutation causes a frame-shift that introduces a premature stop codon.
source: The deletion, of an adenine, causes a frame-shift that introduces a premature stop codon.
evidence: This is a direct consequence of the single base pair deletion identified by sequencing.

claim: WizMommeD30/MommeD30 embryos die around mid-gestation.
source: WizMommeD30/MommeD30 embryos die around mid-gestation and heterozygosity for the mutant allele results in approximately half the normal levels of the protein, confirming that WizMommeD30 is a null allele (Daxinger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an observation from breeding experiments reported in the cited reference.

claim: Heterozygosity for the WizMommeD30 allele results in approximately half the normal levels of the protein.
source: WizMommeD30/MommeD30 embryos die around mid-gestation and heterozygosity for the mutant allele results in approximately half the normal levels of the protein, confirming that WizMommeD30 is a null allele (Daxinger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by protein quantification data from the cited reference.

claim: WizMommeD30 is a null allele.
source: WizMommeD30/MommeD30 embryos die around mid-gestation and heterozygosity for the mutant allele results in approximately half the normal levels of the protein, confirming that WizMommeD30 is a null allele (Daxinger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the premature stop codon, embryonic lethality in homozygotes, and reduced protein levels in heterozygotes.

claim: The WizMommeD30 mouse strain is the only mouse strain with a mutant form of Wiz to be reported.
source: This is the only mouse strain with a mutant form of this gene to be reported.
evidence: This is a claim about the literature at the time of publication.

claim: Wiz protein is predicted to have 11 C2H2 type zinc finger domains that are unusually widely spaced.
source: The protein is predicted to have 11 C2H2 type zinc finger domains that are unusually widely spaced.
evidence: This is based on protein sequence analysis and structural predictions.

claim: Some of Wiz's zinc finger domains can bind DNA.
source: Some of them can bind DNA and some of them can mediate protein-protein interactions with the G9a/GLP (G9a-like) histone methyltransferase complex (Ueda et al., 2006; Bian et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from cited references.

claim: Some of Wiz's zinc finger domains can mediate protein-protein interactions with the G9a/GLP histone methyltransferase complex.
source: Some of them can bind DNA and some of them can mediate protein-protein interactions with the G9a/GLP (G9a-like) histone methyltransferase complex (Ueda et al., 2006; Bian et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from cited references.

claim: The G9a/GLP heterodimer catalyses the methylation of H3K9me1 and H3K9me2.
source: The G9a/GLP heterodimer catalyses the methylation of H3K9me1 and H3K9me2 (Jenuwein et al., 1998; Tachibana et al., 2001, 2002, 2005), which is associated with transcriptional repression (Barski et al., 2007) and is located on chromatin in broad regions, termed LOCKs (large organized chromatin K9-modifications) (Wen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge from multiple cited references.

claim: H3K9me2 is associated with transcriptional repression.
source: The G9a/GLP heterodimer catalyses the methylation of H3K9me1 and H3K9me2 (Jenuwein et al., 1998; Tachibana et al., 2001, 2002, 2005), which is associated with transcriptional repression (Barski et al., 2007) and is located on chromatin in broad regions, termed LOCKs (large organized chromatin K9-modifications) (Wen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: H3K9me2 is located on chromatin in broad regions termed LOCKs (large organized chromatin K9-modifications).
source: The G9a/GLP heterodimer catalyses the methylation of H3K9me1 and H3K9me2 (Jenuwein et al., 1998; Tachibana et al., 2001, 2002, 2005), which is associated with transcriptional repression (Barski et al., 2007) and is located on chromatin in broad regions, termed LOCKs (large organized chromatin K9-modifications) (Wen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: Wiz can stabilize the G9a/GLP complex.
source: Work carried out in cell lines has shown that Wiz can stabilize the G9a/GLP complex, mediate its localisation to DNA and is required for maintaining normal global levels of H3K9me2, suggesting a role in transcriptional repression (Bian et al., 2015; Simon et al., 2015; Ueda et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from cited cell line studies.

claim: Wiz can mediate G9a/GLP localisation to DNA.
source: Work carried out in cell lines has shown that Wiz can stabilize the G9a/GLP complex, mediate its localisation to DNA and is required for maintaining normal global levels of H3K9me2, suggesting a role in transcriptional repression (Bian et al., 2015; Simon et al., 2015; Ueda et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from cited cell line studies.

claim: Wiz is required for maintaining normal global levels of H3K9me2.
source: Work carried out in cell lines has shown that Wiz can stabilize the G9a/GLP complex, mediate its localisation to DNA and is required for maintaining normal global levels of H3K9me2, suggesting a role in transcriptional repression (Bian et al., 2015; Simon et al., 2015; Ueda et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from cited cell line studies.

claim: G9a can act as a transcriptional activator, independent of its histone methyltransferase activity.
source: It has also been shown that G9a can act as a transcriptional activator, independent of its histone methytransferase activity (Chaturvedi et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2006; Oh et al., 2014; Purcell et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2007) and it has recently been suggested that WIZ has a role in the activation function of G9a (Simon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established by multiple cited references.

claim: WIZ has a role in the activation function of G9a.
source: It has also been shown that G9a can act as a transcriptional activator, independent of its histone methytransferase activity (Chaturvedi et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2006; Oh et al., 2014; Purcell et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2007) and it has recently been suggested that WIZ has a role in the activation function of G9a (Simon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is suggested by the cited reference.

claim: Mice heterozygous for the WizMommeD30 allele showed decreased expression of the GFP transgene.
source: WizMommeD30 was identified in the screen because mice heterozygous for the mutant allele showed decreased expression of the GFP transgene.
evidence: This is the observation that led to identification of the mutation in the screen.

claim: Haploinsufficiency for Wiz results in decreased expression at the Agouti viable yellow (Avy) allele.
source: Here, we show at an independent locus known to be sensitive to the dosage of epigenetic modifiers, the Agouti viable yellow (Avy) allele, that haploinsufficiency for Wiz also results in decreased expression.
evidence: This is supported by coat color analysis data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Wiz is expressed highly in the brain, both in the embryo and in the adult.
source: Wiz is expressed highly in the brain, both in the embryo and in the adult (Matsumoto et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established by the cited reference.

claim: Reduced levels of G9a/GLP result in the neurological disease Kleefstra syndrome.
source: As reduced levels of G9a/GLP are known to result in the neurological disease Kleefstra syndrome (Kleefstra et al., 2006; Willemsen et al., 2011), it is possible that reduced levels of Wiz might have neurological consequences.
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references.

claim: Kleefstra syndrome individuals display anxiety.
source: Kleefstra syndrome individuals display a complex range of neurological symptoms, including anxiety (Willemsen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established from the cited clinical reference.

claim: Wiz binds tens of thousands of transcriptional regulatory regions across the genome.
source: Our results show that Wiz binds tens of thousands of transcriptional regulatory regions across the genome, some of which decrease in expression in WizMommeD30/+ tissue.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing approximately 40,000 peaks.

claim: Some Wiz-bound regions decrease in expression in WizMommeD30/+ tissue.
source: Our results show that Wiz binds tens of thousands of transcriptional regulatory regions across the genome, some of which decrease in expression in WizMommeD30/+ tissue.
evidence: This is supported by integration of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: ChIP-seq with an anti-Wiz antibody has been reported in a human kidney cell line.
source: ChIP-seq, with an anti-Wiz antibody, has been reported in a human kidney cell line (Bian et al., 2015) and there is little overlap with our findings.
evidence: This is a reference to published work.

claim: There is little overlap between Wiz ChIP-seq findings in human kidney cells and mouse cerebellum.
source: ChIP-seq, with an anti-Wiz antibody, has been reported in a human kidney cell line (Bian et al., 2015) and there is little overlap with our findings.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the published dataset with the current study's data.

claim: WizMommeD30/+ mice display an anxiety-like phenotype.
source: Our molecular studies prompted us to assess behaviour in heterozygous mutant mice and we found that WizMommeD30/+ mice display an anxiety-like phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data from elevated plus maze and light-dark box tests.

claim: WizMommeD30/+ offspring displayed a shift towards silencing at the Avy locus compared to Wiz+/+ littermates.
source: WizMommeD30/+ offspring from both crosses displayed a shift towards silencing (i.e. more pseudoagouti mice), compared to Wiz+/+ littermates.
evidence: This is supported by coat color scoring data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The shift towards silencing at Avy in offspring from WizMommeD30/+ sire cross had a p-value of 0.0002.
source: The shift was statistically significant in both cases; the shift from WizMommeD30/+ sire cross had a p-value of 0.0002, and from the WizMommeD30/+ dam cross had a p-value of 0.0458 (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is the result of statistical analysis of the coat color data.

claim: The shift towards silencing at Avy in offspring from WizMommeD30/+ dam cross had a p-value of 0.0458.
source: The shift was statistically significant in both cases; the shift from WizMommeD30/+ sire cross had a p-value of 0.0002, and from the WizMommeD30/+ dam cross had a p-value of 0.0458 (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is the result of statistical analysis of the coat color data.

claim: The effect of haploinsufficiency at the Avy locus is similar to the effect at the GFP transgene reporter.
source: The effect of haploinsufficiency at the Avy locus is similar to the effect at the GFP transgene reporter, i.e. reduced levels of Wiz were associated with increased silencing.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparing results from two different reporter systems.

claim: The anti-Wiz antibody (NBP180586) is specific for Wiz in mouse tissue.
source: The bands detected in the wildtype sample (at around 100 kDa) were absent in the sample from the homozygous mutant, consistent with an antibody that is specific for Wiz.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data comparing wildtype and WizMommeD30/MommeD30 samples.

claim: A larger ~160 KDa Wiz isoform has been reported in adult cerebellum.
source: A larger ~160 KDa isoform has previously been reported in adult cerebellum (Matsumoto et al., 1998), and consistent with that report, a band of this size is detected with our antibody in protein extracted from this tissue (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established by the cited reference and confirmed by Western blot data.

claim: Four members of the Wiz-Zfp644-EHMT1-EHMT2 complex were in the top five proteins in the Co-IP dataset from embryonic brain.
source: Four members of the Wiz-Zfp644-EHMT1-EHMT2 complex (Ueda et al., 2006; Bian et al., 2015) were in the top five proteins in the dataset, ranked by peptide count in embryonic brain (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data from co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Approximately 40,000 peaks were identified at which Wiz ChIP-seq datasets were significantly enriched compared to Input control with a p-value of ≤1 × 10−20.
source: Approximately 40,000 peaks were identified at which the two Wiz-ChIP-seq datasets were significantly enriched compared to the Input control with a p-value of ≤1 × 10−20 (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is the result of ChIP-seq peak calling analysis.

claim: Wiz peaks are roughly equally distributed across promoters, intragenic and intergenic regions.
source: The peaks were roughly equally distributed across promoters (defined as 2 kb up and downstream of the TSS), intragenic and intergenic regions, despite the fact that promoters comprise only a small fraction of the total mouse genome (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of ChIP-seq peak locations relative to gene annotations.

claim: Wiz ChIP-seq shows strong enrichment at the TSS.
source: Consistent with this, the deep sequencing read density across the body of all Ensembl genes (normalized for gene length; see Materials and methods), as well as 2 kb upstream of the TSS (transcription start site) and downstream of the TTS (transcriptional termination site), showed strong enrichment at the TSS (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by read density analysis shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: One Wiz motif (Wiz motif 1) had a MEME-ChIP E-value of 2.3 × 10−6903.
source: One of these, Wiz motif 1, had a significance (MEME-ChIP E-value) E-Value of 2.3 × 10−6903, an order of magnitude higher than other motifs and aligned almost perfectly with the CTCF-DNA binding motif (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is the result of motif discovery analysis using MEME-ChIP.

claim: Wiz motif 1 aligned almost perfectly with the CTCF-DNA binding motif.
source: One of these, Wiz motif 1, had a significance (MEME-ChIP E-value) E-Value of 2.3 × 10−6903, an order of magnitude higher than other motifs and aligned almost perfectly with the CTCF-DNA binding motif (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by motif alignment analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Wiz motif 1 was present in approximately 70% of all Wiz binding peaks across the genome.
source: This motif was present in approximately 70% of all Wiz binding peaks across the genome.
evidence: This is the result of motif occurrence analysis in ChIP-seq peaks.

claim: Over half of Wiz ChIP-seq peaks overlapped the promoter mark H3K4me3.
source: Over half of Wiz ChIP-seq peaks overlapped the promoter mark H3K4me3 and approximately a third of all Wiz ChIP-seq peaks overlapped CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by overlap analysis of ChIP-seq peaks shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Approximately a third of all Wiz ChIP-seq peaks overlapped CTCF ChIP-seq peaks.
source: Over half of Wiz ChIP-seq peaks overlapped the promoter mark H3K4me3 and approximately a third of all Wiz ChIP-seq peaks overlapped CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by overlap analysis of ChIP-seq peaks shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Virtually all locations with both CTCF and H3K4me3 peaks also showed a Wiz peak (1356/1359).
source: Virtually all locations with both CTCF and H3K4me3 peaks also showed a Wiz peak (1356/1359).
evidence: This is supported by overlap analysis of ChIP-seq peaks.

claim: Almost all CTCF peaks overlapped with Wiz peaks.
source: Interestingly, almost all CTCF peaks overlapped with Wiz peaks.
evidence: This is supported by overlap analysis of ChIP-seq peaks shown in Figure 3D.

claim: A total of 36 genes were found to change significantly in expression in male E13.5 brains.
source: A total of 36 were found to change in males and 44 changed in females.
evidence: This is the result of RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: A total of 44 genes were found to change significantly in expression in female E13.5 brains.
source: A total of 36 were found to change in males and 44 changed in females.
evidence: This is the result of RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: The majority of significantly differentially expressed genes decreased in expression in the mutants in male E13.5 brains (31/36).
source: The majority of significantly differentially expressed genes, in both cases, decreased in expression in the mutants (31/36 in males and 43/44 in females).
evidence: This is the result of RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: The majority of significantly differentially expressed genes decreased in expression in the mutants in female E13.5 brains (43/44).
source: The majority of significantly differentially expressed genes, in both cases, decreased in expression in the mutants (31/36 in males and 43/44 in females).
evidence: This is the result of RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: 28 genes were common between male and female E13.5 brains in terms of differential expression.
source: Of the combined set of 80 gene expression changes in males and females, 28 genes were common between the sexes and all of these decreased in WizMommeD30/+ samples compared to wildtype samples (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is the result of comparing differential expression results between sexes.

claim: All 28 genes common between male and female E13.5 brains decreased in WizMommeD30/+ samples compared to wildtype samples.
source: Of the combined set of 80 gene expression changes in males and females, 28 genes were common between the sexes and all of these decreased in WizMommeD30/+ samples compared to wildtype samples (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is the result of RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: A relatively high proportion of significantly differentially expressed genes were from the protocadherin β (Pcdhb) gene cluster on Chromosome 18.
source: Among the significantly differentially expressed genes, a relatively high proportion were from two gene clusters, the protocadherin β (Pcdhb) gene cluster on Chromosome 18 and a second cluster consisting of 2610005L07Rik, 6820431F20Rik, AC152164.1, Gm10557, Gm21092, Gm21769, Gm21811, Gm26804 and Gm6483 on Chromosome 8 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the genomic locations of differentially expressed genes.

claim: A relatively high proportion of significantly differentially expressed genes were from a gene cluster on Chromosome 8 consisting of 2610005L07Rik, 6820431F20Rik, AC152164.1, Gm10557, Gm21092, Gm21769, Gm21811, Gm26804 and Gm6483.
source: Among the significantly differentially expressed genes, a relatively high proportion were from two gene clusters, the protocadherin β (Pcdhb) gene cluster on Chromosome 18 and a second cluster consisting of 2610005L07Rik, 6820431F20Rik, AC152164.1, Gm10557, Gm21092, Gm21769, Gm21811, Gm26804 and Gm6483 on Chromosome 8 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the genomic locations of differentially expressed genes.

claim: The Chromosome 8 gene cluster is poorly annotated due to a nearby repeated region that has made mapping difficult.
source: The latter cluster is poorly annotated due to a nearby repeated region that has made mapping difficult (Boyle and Ward, 1992).
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in genome annotation, supported by citation.

claim: Most genes in the Chromosome 8 cluster are annotated as cadherin11 pseudogenes.
source: Under the annotations listed in the UCSC genome browser (Karolchik et al., 2003), most are annotated as cadherin11 pseudogenes; all have introns, and some are predicted to be coding.
evidence: This is based on genome browser annotations.

claim: Several significantly differentially expressed genes in E13.5 brain were located near telomeres.
source: No other gene clusters were apparent, though it was noticed that several genes were located near telomeres and four of the significantly differentially expressed genes, Samd11, psid-ps1, psid-ps2 and Csf2ra, are the last gene on the chromosome.
evidence: This is based on analysis of genomic locations of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Four significantly differentially expressed genes (Samd11, psid-ps1, psid-ps2 and Csf2ra) are the last gene on their respective chromosomes.
source: No other gene clusters were apparent, though it was noticed that several genes were located near telomeres and four of the significantly differentially expressed genes, Samd11, psid-ps1, psid-ps2 and Csf2ra, are the last gene on the chromosome.
evidence: This is based on analysis of genomic locations of differentially expressed genes.

claim: A total of 82 genes were significantly differentially expressed in adult male cerebellum.
source: A total of 82 genes were significantly differentially expressed; 29 genes decreased and 53 increased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ samples compared to Wiz+/+ samples (Figure 5A; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is the result of RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: 29 genes decreased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ adult cerebellum compared to Wiz+/+ samples.
source: A total of 82 genes were significantly differentially expressed; 29 genes decreased and 53 increased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ samples compared to Wiz+/+ samples (Figure 5A; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is the result of RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: 53 genes increased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ adult cerebellum compared to Wiz+/+ samples.
source: A total of 82 genes were significantly differentially expressed; 29 genes decreased and 53 increased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ samples compared to Wiz+/+ samples (Figure 5A; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is the result of RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: 13 genes overlapped between those differentially expressed in adult cerebellum and E13.5 brain.
source: Of these, some genes (n = 13) overlapped with those detected in the E13.5 brain data, including some from the protocadherin β cluster, some from the cadherin 11-like cluster, Wiz, Csf2ra and Rps4l (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on comparison of differential expression results between tissues.

claim: All 13 genes that overlapped between adult cerebellum and E13.5 brain decreased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ samples.
source: These all decreased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ cerebellum compared to the Wiz+/+ cerebellum, as they had done in the embryonic brain.
evidence: This is the result of RNA-seq differential expression analysis in both tissues.

claim: Down regulation of protocadherin β genes was more pronounced in the embryonic brain than in the adult cerebellum.
source: In general, the down regulation of protocadherin β genes was more pronounced in the embryonic brain than in the adult cerebellum, where significance was seen for only a minority of the genes in the clusters (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is based on comparison of RNA-seq results between tissues.

claim: Wiz enrichment was detected at all protocadherin β promoters except Pcdhb1.
source: Wiz enrichment was detected at all protocadherin β promoters except Pcdhb1, which is the only protocadherin β gene that lacks a canonical protocadherin promoter sequence (Guo et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Pcdhb1 is the only protocadherin β gene that lacks a canonical protocadherin promoter sequence.
source: Wiz enrichment was detected at all protocadherin β promoters except Pcdhb1, which is the only protocadherin β gene that lacks a canonical protocadherin promoter sequence (Guo et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references.

claim: The greatest Wiz enrichment at the protocadherin β locus was detected at the HS5-1bL enhancer.
source: The greatest enrichment was detected at the HS5-1bL enhancer.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Wiz enrichment at the HS5-1bL enhancer is an order of magnitude higher than that seen at the individual protocadherin promoters.
source: This enrichment at the enhancer is an order of magnitude higher than that seen at the individual promoters, and this might reflect the fact that while single members of the cluster are expressed in individual neurons, the HS5-1bL enhancer is likely to be active in all cell types (Yokota et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Single members of the protocadherin cluster are expressed in individual neurons.
source: This enrichment at the enhancer is an order of magnitude higher than that seen at the individual promoters, and this might reflect the fact that while single members of the cluster are expressed in individual neurons, the HS5-1bL enhancer is likely to be active in all cell types (Yokota et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: The HS5-1bL enhancer is likely to be active in all cell types.
source: This enrichment at the enhancer is an order of magnitude higher than that seen at the individual promoters, and this might reflect the fact that while single members of the cluster are expressed in individual neurons, the HS5-1bL enhancer is likely to be active in all cell types (Yokota et al., 2011).
evidence: This is inferred from the cited reference and the ChIP-seq data.

claim: Genes that decreased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ cerebellum showed high enrichment for Wiz at the TSS.
source: The genes that decreased in expression showed high enrichment for Wiz and some enrichment for CTCF at the TSS (Figure 6C), while genes that increased in expression showed little enrichment for Wiz and no enrichment for CTCF (Figure 6D), suggesting that those showing increased expression were secondary effects (see Discussion).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq read density analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Genes that decreased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ cerebellum showed some enrichment for CTCF at the TSS.
source: The genes that decreased in expression showed high enrichment for Wiz and some enrichment for CTCF at the TSS (Figure 6C), while genes that increased in expression showed little enrichment for Wiz and no enrichment for CTCF (Figure 6D), suggesting that those showing increased expression were secondary effects (see Discussion).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq read density analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Genes that increased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ cerebellum showed little enrichment for Wiz at the TSS.
source: The genes that decreased in expression showed high enrichment for Wiz and some enrichment for CTCF at the TSS (Figure 6C), while genes that increased in expression showed little enrichment for Wiz and no enrichment for CTCF (Figure 6D), suggesting that those showing increased expression were secondary effects (see Discussion).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq read density analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Genes that increased in expression in WizMommeD30/+ cerebellum showed no enrichment for CTCF at the TSS.
source: The genes that decreased in expression showed high enrichment for Wiz and some enrichment for CTCF at the TSS (Figure 6C), while genes that increased in expression showed little enrichment for Wiz and no enrichment for CTCF (Figure 6D), suggesting that those showing increased expression were secondary effects (see Discussion).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq read density analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Genes showing increased expression in WizMommeD30/+ cerebellum are likely secondary effects.
source: The genes that decreased in expression showed high enrichment for Wiz and some enrichment for CTCF at the TSS (Figure 6C), while genes that increased in expression showed little enrichment for Wiz and no enrichment for CTCF (Figure 6D), suggesting that those showing increased expression were secondary effects (see Discussion).
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of Wiz binding at genes with increased expression.

claim: WizMommeD30/+ mice showed decreased activity in the first two hours after lights off compared with Wiz+/+ mice.
source: No shift was seen in the circadian pattern, but decreased activity was seen in the first two hours and the fifth hour after lights off in WizMommeD30/+ mice compared with the Wiz+/+ mice (Figure 7A; time x genotype interaction, F(23, 391) = 3.923, p<0.001, ε = 0.350).
evidence: This is supported by telemetry monitoring data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: WizMommeD30/+ mice showed decreased activity in the fifth hour after lights off compared with Wiz+/+ mice.
source: No shift was seen in the circadian pattern, but decreased activity was seen in the first two hours and the fifth hour after lights off in WizMommeD30/+ mice compared with the Wiz+/+ mice (Figure 7A; time x genotype interaction, F(23, 391) = 3.923, p<0.001, ε = 0.350).
evidence: This is supported by telemetry monitoring data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: No difference in temperature profiles was seen in WizMommeD30/+ mice compared to Wiz+/+ mice at any time points.
source: No difference was seen in WizMommeD30/+ mice compared to Wiz+/+ mice at any of the time points (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by telemetry temperature monitoring data.

claim: WizMommeD30/+ mice showed an approximately 25% reduction in the frequency of entry into the open arms of the EPM apparatus compared with Wiz+/+ mice.
source: WizMommeD30/+ showed an approximately 25% reduction in the frequency of entry into the open arms of the EPM apparatus compared with the Wiz+/+ mice (Figure 7B and C; t(17) = 2.90, p=0.010).
evidence: This is supported by elevated plus maze behavioral testing data.

claim: WizMommeD30/+ mice showed reduced time spent in the light in the light-dark box test.
source: WizMommeD30/+ mice showed reduced time spent in the light and reduced rearing activity (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is supported by light-dark box behavioral testing data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: WizMommeD30/+ mice showed reduced rearing activity in the light-dark box test.
source: WizMommeD30/+ mice showed reduced time spent in the light and reduced rearing activity (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: This is supported by light-dark box behavioral testing data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The findings from the light-dark box test are consistent with an anxiety-like phenotype in WizMommeD30/+ mice.
source: These findings are consistent with an anxiety-like phenotype in WizMommeD30/+ mice.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the behavioral data in the context of established anxiety assays.

claim: The WizMommeD30 mutation was the only exonic mutation within the linked interval.
source: This was the only exonic mutation within the linked interval and in agreement with this being the causative MommeD30 mutation, RNA-seq data presented here show no other genes within the linked interval were miss-expressed in mutants.
evidence: This is based on sequencing of the linked interval.

claim: No other genes within the linked interval were miss-expressed in WizMommeD30 mutants.
source: This was the only exonic mutation within the linked interval and in agreement with this being the causative MommeD30 mutation, RNA-seq data presented here show no other genes within the linked interval were miss-expressed in mutants.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Wiz has no recognisable catalytic domains.
source: While Wiz has no recognisable catalytic domains, it does have C2H2-type zinc fingers and these have an unusual widely-spaced configuration (Matsumoto et al., 1998).
evidence: This is based on protein sequence analysis.

claim: Most proteins that contain multiple zinc fingers have them in a cluster with short linker sequences (usually less than 10 amino acids).
source: Most proteins that contain multiple zinc fingers have them in a cluster, with short 'linker' sequences (usually less than 10 amino acids) separating the fingers (Schuh et al., 1986).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: Most Wiz zinc fingers are at least 50 amino acids apart.
source: Most Wiz zinc fingers are at least 50 amino acids apart.
evidence: This is based on protein sequence analysis.

claim: Other zinc finger-containing proteins with widely-spaced configuration include Zfp292, Rlf and the Drosophila protein Su(Var)3–7.
source: Other zinc finger-containing proteins with this configuration include Zfp292, Rlf and the Drosophila protein Su(Var)3–7 and all of these have been shown to bind DNA in vitro using electromobility shift assays (Cléard and Spierer, 2001; Harten et al., 2015; Lipkin et al., 1993).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references.

claim: Zfp292, Rlf and Su(Var)3–7 have all been shown to bind DNA in vitro using electromobility shift assays.
source: Other zinc finger-containing proteins with this configuration include Zfp292, Rlf and the Drosophila protein Su(Var)3–7 and all of these have been shown to bind DNA in vitro using electromobility shift assays (Cléard and Spierer, 2001; Harten et al., 2015; Lipkin et al., 1993).
evidence: This is established by the cited references.

claim: Rlf was identified as an E(Var) in the MommeD screen.
source: Rlf, like Wiz, was identified as an E(Var) in the MommeD screen (Daxinger et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a fact from the cited reference.

claim: Multiple isoforms of Wiz are present in the mouse, three at ~100 kDa and one larger ~160 kDa.
source: Consistent with previous studies using different Wiz antibodies (Matsumoto et al., 1998; Ueda et al., 2006; Ma et al., 2015; Simon et al., 2015) we identified multiple isoforms of Wiz present in the mouse, three at ~100 kDa and one larger ~160 kDa.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data and is consistent with cited references.

claim: G9A can methylate non-histone targets, including Wiz.
source: For example, it is known that G9A can methylate non-histone targets, including Wiz (Rathert et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: CTCF is a recognized transcriptional activator.
source: Our ChIP-seq studies suggest that in adult cerebellum, Wiz binds at promoters and at sites which CTCF, a recognized transcriptional activator, is also known to bind.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CTCF function.

claim: Competitive binding with CTCF and the closely related BORIS has been demonstrated.
source: Competitive binding with CTCF and the closely related BORIS has been demonstrated (Pugacheva et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established by the cited reference.

claim: Wiz has not been pulled down with antibodies to CTCF.
source: To our knowledge, Wiz has not been pulled down with antibodies to CTCF (Xiao et al., 2011; Yusufzai et al., 2004), though a protein-protein interaction is possible in neural cell types where Wiz is expressed highly and co-immunoprecipitation of binding partners remains to be tested.
evidence: This is based on review of the cited literature.

claim: CTCF is enriched at topologically associated domain boundaries.
source: CTCF has multiple roles in organizing the genome; it is enriched at topologically associated domain boundaries and can mediate interactions between an enhancer and promoter elements (Bell et al., 1999; Ong and Corces, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references.

claim: CTCF can mediate interactions between an enhancer and promoter elements.
source: CTCF has multiple roles in organizing the genome; it is enriched at topologically associated domain boundaries and can mediate interactions between an enhancer and promoter elements (Bell et al., 1999; Ong and Corces, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references.

claim: Broad regions marked by H3K9me2 often contain small 'euchromatic islands' that are devoid of H3K9me2, are DNase1 hypersensitive and have CTCF binding.
source: Broad regions marked by H3K9me2 often contain small 'euchromatic islands' that are devoid of H3K9me2, are DNase1 hypersensitive and have CTCF binding (Wen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: Reducing WIZ levels resulted in less G9a at CTCF-binding sites across the genome in human cell lines.
source: A recent study in a number of human cell lines found that reducing WIZ levels resulted in less G9a at CTCF-binding sites across the genome (by carrying out ChIP-seq for G9a) (Simon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established by the cited reference.

claim: Protocadherin genes are expressed mainly in neurons.
source: Protocadherin genes are expressed mainly in neurons (Kohmura et al., 1998; Wu and Maniatis, 1999) and here we report the involvement of Wiz at protocadherin β genes.
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references.

claim: CTCF binds to the promoters and enhancer of the protocadherin β locus, mediating the looping required for the transcription of single protocadherin β genes in single neural cells.
source: CTCF has been shown by others to bind to the promoters and enhancer of this locus, mediating the looping required for the transcription of single protocadherin β genes in single neural cells (Guo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established by the cited reference.

claim: At the protocadherin locus, heterochromatinisation facilitates single isoform expression in single cells.
source: At this locus, heterochromatinisation facilitates single isoform expression in single cells i.e. the silencing of the majority of protocadherin genes in any single cell is associated with heterochromatin formation (Kawaguchi et al., 2008; Toyoda et al., 2014); the expressed loci must remain active despite being embedded in heterochromatin and it is possible that Wiz has a role in this scenario.
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references.

claim: The silencing of the majority of protocadherin genes in any single cell is associated with heterochromatin formation.
source: At this locus, heterochromatinisation facilitates single isoform expression in single cells i.e. the silencing of the majority of protocadherin genes in any single cell is associated with heterochromatin formation (Kawaguchi et al., 2008; Toyoda et al., 2014); the expressed loci must remain active despite being embedded in heterochromatin and it is possible that Wiz has a role in this scenario.
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references.

claim: Wiz may have a role in keeping expressed protocadherin loci active despite being embedded in heterochromatin.
source: At this locus, heterochromatinisation facilitates single isoform expression in single cells i.e. the silencing of the majority of protocadherin genes in any single cell is associated with heterochromatin formation (Kawaguchi et al., 2008; Toyoda et al., 2014); the expressed loci must remain active despite being embedded in heterochromatin and it is possible that Wiz has a role in this scenario.
evidence: This is speculation based on the ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Many enzymes that modify histones and DNA have been found to be critical for development and function of the brain.
source: The importance of epigenetic modifications in neural function is emerging; many enzymes that modify histones and DNA have been found to be critical for development and function of the brain.
evidence: This is general knowledge about the field of neuroepigenetics.

claim: Prior to this study, no link between Wiz and behaviour had been shown in either mice or humans.
source: Prior to this study, no link between Wiz and behaviour had been shown in either mice or humans.
evidence: This is a claim about the state of the literature.

claim: Heterozygosity for rare WIZ mutations in humans could influence neurological disorders that have a complex genetic aetiology.
source: It is possible that heterozygosity for rare WIZ mutations in humans could influence neurological disorders that have a complex genetic aetiology.
evidence: This is speculation based on the mouse behavioral findings.

claim: Mice with reduced expression of protocadherin β genes due to knockout of CTCF have disorganized formation of the barrel cortex.
source: Mice with reduced expression of protocadherin β genes, due to knockout of CTCF (Hirayama et al., 2012) or the downstream enhancer (Yokota et al., 2011), have disorganized formation of the barrel cortex, a region of the brain important for processing information for the tactile somatosensory pathway (Petersen, 2007).
evidence: This is established by the cited references.

claim: Mice with reduced expression of protocadherin β genes due to knockout of the downstream enhancer have disorganized formation of the barrel cortex.
source: Mice with reduced expression of protocadherin β genes, due to knockout of CTCF (Hirayama et al., 2012) or the downstream enhancer (Yokota et al., 2011), have disorganized formation of the barrel cortex, a region of the brain important for processing information for the tactile somatosensory pathway (Petersen, 2007).
evidence: This is established by the cited references.

claim: The barrel cortex is a region of the brain important for processing information for the tactile somatosensory pathway.
source: Mice with reduced expression of protocadherin β genes, due to knockout of CTCF (Hirayama et al., 2012) or the downstream enhancer (Yokota et al., 2011), have disorganized formation of the barrel cortex, a region of the brain important for processing information for the tactile somatosensory pathway (Petersen, 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the cited reference.

claim: Over 30 million reads were generated for each of the two Wiz ChIP-seq datasets and the chromatin Input sample dataset.
source: Over 30 million reads were generated for each of the two Wiz ChIP-seq datasets and the chromatin Input sample dataset.
evidence: This is a description of the sequencing depth achieved.

claim: At least 24 million reads could be aligned to the mouse mm10 genome in all ChIP-seq cases, after filtering out PCR duplicates.
source: At least 24 million reads could be aligned to the mouse mm10 genome in all cases, after filtering out PCR duplicates.
evidence: This is a description of the alignment results.

claim: Wiz ChIP-qPCR validated enrichment at a representative Wiz peak.
source: A representative Wiz peak and ChIP-qPCR validation at the same locus is shown in Figure 2A and B, respectively.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B which displays ChIP-qPCR enrichment at the peak location.

claim: WizMommeD30/+ offspring from crosses with WizMommeD30/+ sire showed a statistically significant shift towards silencing at Avy (p=0.0002).
source: The shift was statistically significant in both cases; the shift from WizMommeD30/+ sire cross had a p-value of 0.0002, and from the WizMommeD30/+ dam cross had a p-value of 0.0458 (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A with statistical analysis.

claim: WizMommeD30/+ offspring from crosses with WizMommeD30/+ dam showed a statistically significant shift towards silencing at Avy (p=0.0458).
source: The shift was statistically significant in both cases; the shift from WizMommeD30/+ sire cross had a p-value of 0.0002, and from the WizMommeD30/+ dam cross had a p-value of 0.0458 (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B with statistical analysis.
